decisions: Do not claim Sloar can cancel, finish, or revive a host response that remains stuck in an answering state.
Engineering terminality and user-visible response delivery are separate facts.
Elapsed wall-clock time alone never proves an old host process is dead; takeover requires explicit user intent.
Takeover increments a monotonic fencing epoch; active turns using this contract verify turn_id plus epoch before later guarded durable writes/publication.
Fencing cannot retroactively cancel a write already in flight before the epoch changed.
Repository current state, last verified state, and serving runtime may use separate evidence-backed anchors.
Reuse target-repository current-status/history/ADR conventions when present instead of imposing parallel Sloar product-history files.
Evidence type and scope must match the claim; CI green is not universal proof of visual, integration, or production health.
Target repository engineering policy remains authoritative; Flow-specific Blank app rules were not absorbed into Sloar.
